overview: A second `Ctrl-C` while `Command.main()` was printing `Aborted!` or an error used to escape as a traceback, because the message and `sys.exit()` ran inside `except` clauses. Now every handler only records a message and an exit code, and one teardown step reports and exits under an outer handler, so a late interrupt can cost the message but never the exit code.

components.name: `Command.main()`
behavior: A late `KeyboardInterrupt` in standalone mode exits with the code already collected: `1` for aborts, the error's `exit_code`, `0` after success
Without standalone mode, the late interrupt propagates to the caller instead of becoming `exit 1`
The first interrupt still reaches non-standalone callers as `Abort` with the interrupt as `__cause__`

components.name: docs
behavior: `docs/exceptions.md` replaces the numbered list with a table of every way a command ends, and shows how to replace the `Aborted!` message

walkthrough.text:
### What and why

Issue [#3802](https://github.com/pallets/click/issues/3802): pressing `Ctrl-C` a second time while Click reports an abort or an error printed a traceback, since the reporting ran in `except` clauses that no `try` covered. The PR applies the policy the pager has had since #351: **a late interrupt must not replace the intended outcome**.

### One teardown instead of exits in every handler

Each `except` clause in `Command.main()` now does the same two things: re-raise when `standalone_mode` is off, otherwise set `report` and `exit_code`. The `Exit` handler moves into the inner `try`, which removes one nesting level.

After the inner `try`, the teardown calls `report()` and `sys.exit(exit_code)`. The outer `except (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt)` catches an interrupt that lands there and exits with the code that was already chosen. Check that `exit_code` is set before anything that can be interrupted: it starts at `1`, and success reaches the teardown through `ctx.exit()`, which sets it to `0`.
The `Aborted!` message moves into a small helper, so the two abort paths can store it as `report` without calling it yet.

### Tests

The new tests fake a second interrupt at each point that can be interrupted: `RecordingStderr` raises from its `N`-th `isatty()` call, which `echo()` makes before writing; others patch `ClickException.show()`, `Abort.__init__` or `sys.exit()`.

### Before merging

- After success, a late interrupt now exits `0` instead of printing a traceback; the PR asks maintainers to confirm this policy.
- The PR description mentions stress tests with real `SIGINT`s and random delays; the diff only has the monkeypatched tests.
